# conjur_issuer (Resource)

CyberArk Secrets Manager issuer resource. Destroying this resource deletes only the issuer itself and leaves the referenced Secrets Manager secrets intact.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "conjur_issuer" "my_aws_issuer" {
  id      = "my-aws-issuer"
  max_ttl = 3600

  aws = {
    access_key_id_secret_ref     = "data/terraform/aws-access-key-id"
    secret_access_key_secret_ref = "data/terraform/aws-secret-access-key"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) The issuer's name. Changing it forces a new issuer to be created.
- `max_ttl` (Number) The maximum time-to-live, in seconds, of dynamic secrets created with this issuer. Must be between `900` and `43200`, and cannot be decreased once the issuer exists.

### Optional

- `aws` (Attributes) Configuration for an AWS issuer. Exactly one issuer type block must be specified at a time. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--aws))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) The timestamp at which the issuer was created.
- `modified_at` (String) The timestamp at which the issuer was last modified.

<a id="nestedatt--aws"></a>
### Nested Schema for `aws`

Required:

- `access_key_id_secret_ref` (String) The identifier of the Secrets Manager secret that holds the AWS access key ID.
- `secret_access_key_secret_ref` (String) The identifier of the Secrets Manager secret that holds the AWS secret access key.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import conjur_issuer.my_aws_issuer my-aws-issuer
```
